hook_text: Fifteen ledger accounts, two columns, one test. If the totals match, the double entry worked.
clip_script: Thirtieth of April. Every ledger folder has one balance on its front. Copy them onto one page. Left column, debit: bank eighty thousand one hundred and eighty-five, equipment twenty-three thousand two hundred, drawings, and every expense. Right column, credit: capital seventy thousand, loan twenty-five thousand, and every income. Add the left: one hundred and thirty-four thousand eight hundred and eighty. Add the right: one hundred and thirty-four thousand eight hundred and eighty. It balances, because every transaction went in twice, once on each side. But careful: a forgotten transaction would still balance. And the bonus? Income minus expenses: a profit of thirteen thousand eight hundred and eighty-five rand.
visual_style: A whiteboard page with two columns filling up line by line from labelled T-account folders, ending in matching totals with double underlines.
mood: Tense build-up, then a satisfying match.
pacing: Quick listing of balances, a pause before the two totals, then a fast warning and profit reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw up the trial balance yourself.
